Year 2 Semester 2 · Capstone Project

GorkhaSEC Research

Published · October 2025 · WSU

Simulated Stress Analysis in Incident Response

A research-driven capstone investigating how Security Operations Center (SOC) automated pipelines perform under simultaneous, high-volume cyberattacks. The project built a full virtual SOC environment and stress-tested its incident response systems under realistic attack conditions.

Key outcome: concurrent attack campaigns measurably degrade automation — triage latency increased 40%, CPU utilisation peaked at 78%, and false positives nearly doubled. The team proposed the Stress-Resilient Incident Response (SRIR) framework to address these failures.

VirtualBoxKali LinuxMetasploitSplunk EnterpriseWiresharkSecurity OnionProcess Explorertcpdump
Company
GorkhaSEC
Supervisor
Robert Beutel
Institution
Western Sydney University
Team
4 researchers

Key Research Findings

01

Automation Fragility Under Stress

40% increase in triage latency and near-double false positives during concurrent multi-vector attacks — contradicting the assumption that automation relieves pressure.

02

Hybrid Telemetry Has Scalability Limits

Process Explorer + PCAP gave high-fidelity forensic data but required manual correlation — creating an analyst bottleneck at scale.

03

Stealth Attack Detection Gaps

In-memory and non-persistent attacks evaded detection, revealing that SOC visibility depends on telemetry breadth, not alert volume.

04

SRIR Framework Proposed

Recommended alert deduplication, adaptive correlation thresholds, load-aware automation tiers, and digital-twin CI/CD rehearsal to engineer resilience into SOC pipelines.
